doc.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: CTI, Compost and the first Directions
title: How Compost got its name
summary: The band chose Compost because good things grow from it, like their mix of jazz, rock and soul.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I just want to go back and just a couple things I want to talk about, you’re (philosophy) about “multi-directions,” which impacts what you base the name of your group on, but also let’s briefly go back to Compost because I had the album and I remember there was a definition of “compost” on the back, and it said, “earthy.” So who chose the name?

We talked about Compost as… things came from compost. Good things came from that. It was kind of funky. We thought, “Compost, it’s kind of what this band it is.” It’s kind of a potpourri of mixes of things: Jazz, rock, some soul and some free- form things. We kind of all agreed that Compost felt nice. It’s a funny name, but we need
compost to grow vegetables and things. A lot of stuff that ferments and changes is good for the soil, so that’s how we decided what came out of this mix was some good compost music. HOUR 5
